note: Estonia: EEA and Swiss nationals live and work freely (the eea list). An alien staying temporarily may work only once the employer has registered the short-term employment with the Police and Border Guard Board, or on a temporary residence permit for employment, except where the law gives the right: among those cases, temporary work of no more than five days within 30 (Aliens Act §§ 104(2) and 105(4) clause 3). Read from Riigi Teataja's English translation of the text in force from 1 January 2026, the latest found. Route corrected 2026-11-01 from the permit research (papers.permits.EE): it was “Temporary residence permit for employment”.

sources.title: Riigi Teataja, Aliens Act (English translation, in force from 1 January 2026), §§ 104, 105 and 177
sources.said: An alien who is staying temporarily in Estonia is prohibited to take employment in Estonia if his or her employer has failed to register his or her short-term employment in the Police and Border Guard Board except in the cases prescribed in a treaty ratified by the Riigikogu or in the cases prescribed by law. ... An alien may take employment in Estonia without a residence permit issued for employment if he or she: ... who has a legal basis for the stay in Estonia, whose employment is of temporary nature and whose term of employment does not exceed five days within the period of 30 days; ... The purpose of the granting of a temporary residence permit is to further the development of the Estonian economy, research, education or culture by creating a possibility to employ aliens with the necessary knowledge and skills in Estonia.
